heading: SVX2 FastROM Animated Video
lede: Two complete Artemis videos: 600 frames of NASA SVS launch-and-return animation followed by 300 frames of real launch-camera footage, decoded at a verified 30 fps from a 4 MiB Fast HiROM.
keysHtml: Self-running — begins playback in under four seconds, then switches to an independent codec keyframe at the frame-600 cut.
doc:
Two videos, one cartridge

Frames 0–599 are NASA SVS Artemis animation; frames 600–899 are real launch-camera footage. They use independent keyframes and one palette learned across the complete 900-frame reel.

Fast start

Playback begins in under four seconds. Exhaustive 900-frame validation runs at build time rather than behind the title.

Cartridge-native dashboard

Mode 7 video occupies scanlines 0–191; Mode 1 BG3 renders TIME, measured FPS, and health below. The shared palette eliminates runtime CGRAM transitions, keeping the HDMA split and dashboard continuously active across both video cuts.

30 fps full-pipeline result

The regression records 1,909 presentations in 4,000 VBlanks, covers two complete loops, and reports zero decoder errors and zero deadline slips. Separate animation and real-camera screenshot gates require visible dashboard text, while the full-run blank scan rejects transient black frames.

Sources: NASA SVS 14191 animation and NASA Artemis I press-site camera footage. No Duck and Cover footage is present.
